title: (hitch, Direct3D 12) a Present waits for every pipeline creation in flight (core/present_gate.h, the guard against a driver trimming its pipeline cache inside Present), so one slow creation holds the picture: quick gate of aa05466af, engine/save-newer, no frame for 26 s at frame 596 with the machine loaded (nebula-hang dump: render thread in present_to_swap_chain on gPresentGate, pipeline workers in Pipelines::build); the same test alone on the same bins, 3 of 3 pass (02:55, with another gate running)
note: What it costs a player: the length of the slowest creation in flight, each time a Present falls while one runs; with a warm pipeline library a load is under a millisecond, a cold creation tens to hundreds of milliseconds, so first sightings of a material in play hitch. Design: no creation in flight during play, which is E5's first item (every pipeline a stage needs built while it loads, P-010, P-052): the gate then never waits outside a load screen. Until then the gate's wait is logged when it passes one frame (timeline event), so a tour shows each. The guard stays for every device (no device names); closes with P-010/P-052 and a tour whose timeline has no gate wait after the first picture of a stage. Seen again 11-18 with no second gate on the machine (Agent 3's two game-module builds ran, 4 jobs): main gate of fc23ce733, at 03:19, tour-RMGJ01/025-EggStarGalaxy-4 d3d12, the game's probes not back within 2 s at frame 564 (4.1 to 6.1 s) while 30 workers prepared 6466 pipelines against a new driver cache (done at 5879 ms, 88 made by draws first): the start's set ran into play because a deterministic run's title does not wait for it (host_main.cpp:3346-3354, NEBULA_OPTION_PREPARATION: the frames waited would differ by machine), while a player's title waits on a cold cache. So in a test every Present of the first seconds can wait on the gate; for a player only creations made in play do (draws first, a later settings change). That is what a test's late probes then meet; the timeline event (above) names each such wait.

title: (performance) A draw whose pipeline is not made yet compiles it on the render thread; only Vulkan with graphics pipeline libraries gets a quick link.
note: Design (read 11-18, E5's first item, with P-052 and N-1067): a stage's pipelines are made while it loads, and a draw never compiles. (1) Pipelines are registered as the stage's materials register (registries_, game thread, during the load); the render thread queues the new ones each frame (render_core.cpp, pipelines_queued_) for low-priority workers. The game's load already ends at one gate, GameSystemSceneController::isReadyToStartScene (the load screen's nerve waits there for the scene's worker): it also asks the host that every pipeline registered so far is made (Pipelines::pending() for the set queued, the workers raised to normal priority while the game waits). The load screen keeps stepping as it does for the scene's own load. (2) A draw whose pipeline is still missing in play (a material registered after the load, a settings change) is skipped for that frame and its job moved to the front of the queue at normal priority, never built on the render thread; Vulkan with pipeline libraries keeps its quick link. A miss is a timeline event and counted (made by draws first stays 0 after a stage's first picture). Proof: a tour on a cold cache (the cache files removed) on D3D12, Vulkan and the tablet: no create_now build on the render thread after a stage's first picture, frame times at first entry to three galaxies against today's, pictures the same, step-hash replays the same.

title: (performance, first use) Utility pipelines are compiled on the render thread at first use, outside the pipeline cache.
note: Design (read 11-18): renderer_d3d12.cpp creates its utility pipelines (post-process, bloom, present, conversion; 22 CreateGraphicsPipelineState/CreateComputePipelineState calls) directly, outside the driver cache (core/pipelines_d3d12.cpp's ID3D12PipelineLibrary), at first use on the render thread. They are made at initialize on the pipeline workers through the same library (named entries, so a warm run loads them), and the per-sample forms for every sample count the settings offer; Metal's are P-065, D3D11's are made at initialize already. Proof: a cold and a warm start, D3D12 timeline: no utility pipeline made on the render thread; the warm start loads every one from the library. First half built 11-18 (412007306): core::utility_pipeline loads and stores the renderer's 22 pipelines in the driver cache by a hash of every field (Vulkan's post, mod post and SGSR2 pass the shared cache). Test: post_process_tests utility_pipelines_on_warp (a second PostProcessor loads, makes none). Second half written (each pass's prepare_pipelines for every sample count at the start, on threads of their own; Vulkan's scene camera keyed by render pass, as its pass changes with HDR output), applied after the first half is proved. Second half built (eeebb5dbc): post_process_tests prepared_pipelines_on_warp (a prepare makes 2 x the supported sample counts, a second makes none, set_wide adds the six chain pipelines and the float scene's pairs), the MSAA 4x stage run logs every pass pipeline at the start and none after; the D3D12 tour's pictures 408 of 408 the same as b865c09e8's. Closes with the main gate.

title: performance (hitches; Metal): the renderer's own shaders are compiled from MSL source on the render thread the first time each is used
note: Design (read 11-18): the game's programs already ship as bytecode (platform/apple/tools/compile_metallib.py, programs_2_4/3_0.metallib), but the renderer's own shaders are texts made by C++ (utility_msl, post_msl by program and quality, metalfx's kDepthCopy) compiled with newLibraryWithSource at first use in eight files (ambient_occlusion, game_bloom, metalfx, pipelines_mtl:283, post_process, renderer_mtl_scene, scene_camera, sgsr2). New: a build step runs a small host program that writes every such text (each variant by its parameters) to utility_msl.bin; compile_metallib.py compiles it into utility.metallib beside the programs' libraries, each text a function named by its hash; at run time the text is still made, hashed, and its function taken from the bundle's library, with newLibraryWithSource only when the library lacks it (a build without Xcode), which is logged. Their pipeline states are then made on a worker at renderer start, as P-052 does for D3D12. Proof (Apple is compile-only for now): the macOS build job's log names 0 texts left to compile in a start check, and a test compares utility_msl.bin's hashes with the texts the runtime makes.
